skill.name: to-questionnaire
skill.description: Create a focused Markdown questionnaire when another person holds the facts needed for a decision.
skill.summary: Turn an information gap into a clear questionnaire for the right recipient.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code delimiters. The skill only guides creation of a local questionnaire and shows no prompt-injection, data-exfiltration, or command-execution intent.

static_findings.snippet: 3. **Write the questionnaire.** Draft questions aimed at the gap from steps 1–2, following the Docum
Frame the document as a **discovery questionnaire**: the user lacks context, the recipient holds it.
One `##` section per theme. Under each, its questions, most-important-first. Every question is one i

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit a Markdown filename, not executable shell or Ruby syntax. The instruction describes writing a document and contains no command execution.
The backticks delimit a Markdown heading marker in prose. No shell command, interpreter call, or executable content is present.
The backticks quote the Markdown section syntax `##` as documentation. This is not Ruby or shell backtick execution.

content.value_statement: Important decisions can stall when one person lacks key context. This skill creates a focused questionnaire that helps the informed recipient provide the needed facts.
actual_capabilities: Asks who will receive the questionnaire and what knowledge they hold.
Clarifies the decisions or facts the user needs from the recipient.
Drafts questions that target the identified information gap.
Organizes questions by theme and places the most important questions first.
Includes context, answer guidance, and a closing catch-all question.
Writes the questionnaire to a Markdown file in the current directory.
limitations: It cannot verify whether the recipient answers accurately or completely.
It requires the user to identify the recipient and the needed outcome.
It creates a questionnaire, not a final decision or implementation plan.
It does not send the questionnaire or manage responses.

use_cases.title: Clarify product requirements
use_cases.description: Prepare focused questions for a product stakeholder before a feature decision.

use_cases.title: Gather system context
use_cases.description: Ask a system owner for operational facts needed to plan a technical change.

use_cases.title: Prepare client discovery
use_cases.description: Create an async questionnaire that collects client goals, constraints, and priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Start a questionnaire
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a questionnaire for a decision I cannot answer alone.

prompt_templates.title: Ask a colleague
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a questionnaire for my operations colleague. I need to learn the deployment constraints for a new service.
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect facts from an internal expert.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare client discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a questionnaire for a new client. I need their goals, target users, timeline, budget constraints, and approval process.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a technical migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a questionnaire for the database owner. I need the current workload, data retention rules, downtime tolerance, integrations, recovery requirements, and migration approval criteria.

output_examples.input: Create questions for an infrastructure owner about launch capacity.
output: A purpose statement tied to the launch decision.
Questions about expected load, traffic peaks, capacity limits, and monitoring.
Answer stubs and explanations for questions that need extra context.

output_examples.input: Create a questionnaire for a client about a website redesign.
output: A short context section for the client.
Themed questions about audiences, content, brand, deadlines, and approvals.
A final catch-all question for missing information.

best_practices: Name one recipient who has direct knowledge of the information gap.
State the decision or action the answers must enable.
Review the questions before sending and remove duplicate or compound questions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask broad questions without explaining the decision they support.
Do not combine several unrelated facts into one question.
Do not treat the questionnaire as a substitute for validating important answers.

faq.question: Who should receive the questionnaire?
faq.answer: Send it to a person who directly holds the facts or expertise you need.

faq.question: Can I use this during a meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. You can fill it out together during a meeting or send it for an async response.

faq.question: What does the skill ask first?
faq.answer: It asks about the recipient and the decisions or facts you need back.

faq.question: What format does it create?
faq.answer: It creates a Markdown questionnaire with context, themed questions, and answer stubs.

faq.question: Will it send the questionnaire?
faq.answer: No. It writes a local Markdown file and reports its path.

faq.question: Can it make the decision for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps collect missing information so you can make the decision.
